_doc._description: optitrack_zmq_bridge --map-config for the real Motive setup (see MPC/config/mocap_config.txt for the matching --mocap-config connection settings). Loaded by mpc::load_map_config(); any field not present here falls back to its identity default. Unknown keys (like this one) are ignored, never an error.
_doc.aliases: Round 5: Motive asset name -> published name, used ONLY in auto-discovery mode (the bridge's zero-arg default when --robots is omitted entirely -- see optitrack_zmq_bridge --help). "mushr2" is the real Motive asset name of the user's actual robot (discovered via the bridge's one-time 'Motive assets: ...' inventory log on a first live run); aliasing it to "robot1" keeps the published ZMQ topic name (/robot1/localization) matching what the rest of this project's tooling (mpc_controller, MARS, etc.) already expects, without needing --rigid-body-names on every run. Any OTHER rigid body Motive reports (with no alias entry) still auto-publishes too, under its own sanitized Motive name.
_doc.mocap_to_world_matrix: Round 6: full 2D homogeneous affine transform [[a,b,tx],[c,d,ty],[0,0,1]] from mocap-frame planar pose to world/map-frame planar pose -- SUPERSEDES x0/y0/theta0 above whenever present. [x_w,y_w]=[[a,b],[c,d]]*[x_m,y_m]+[tx,ty]; yaw_w=wrap(atan2(c,a)+yaw_m) (yaw_offset above is added on top of that, same as always). Currently an IDENTITY placeholder -- this is the planner-frame calibration slot: replace it with the measured mocap->world transform once that calibration exists (e.g. by recording a few known-position points in both Motive's frame and the real world/planner frame and solving for [[a,b],[c,d],[tx,ty]]). The bottom row [0,0,1] is validated at load (hard error if wrong); the rotation block should stay a pure rotation (orthonormal, det=+1) -- a scale/shear matrix is still ACCEPTED and fully applied to position, but logs a loud warning since the yaw formula above is then only approximate.
_doc.x0/y0/theta0: The legacy rigid (rotation+translation only) 2D transform from Motive's arbitrary mocap origin into this project's world/map frame (see mpc::apply_planar_transform()). SUPERSEDED by "mocap_to_world_matrix" below whenever that key is present (see its own _doc entry and optitrack_zmq_bridge.cpp's precedence warning) -- kept here at IDENTITY (0,0,0) mainly as a documented fallback/reference, not the active transform. Do not set these to anything nonzero while mocap_to_world_matrix is also present; the bridge will warn and ignore them.
_doc.y_up: CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-04: set back to true -- the user directly confirmed their Motive rig's own convention is Y-up (ground = X-Z plane, +Z is 90deg clockwise from +X viewed from above, +Y is up), which is exactly the bridge's y_up=true code path (planar (x,y)=(raw_x,-raw_z), yaw=atan2(-vz,vx) -- see mpc::quat_to_planar_yaw()/extract_planar_pose()/mocap_rotation()). This OVERRIDES the 2026-08-03 (round 6) y_up:false guess below, which was inferred indirectly from raw-height sign/magnitude heuristics rather than asked of the user directly -- a direct rig-convention confirmation from the user outranks that inference. The round-6 evidence is kept here for history/context only, not as a reason to flip back: (a) round-4's y_up:true reading put a marker's pivot 17cm BELOW the floor (raw_y=-0.169) while raw_z=+0.004 looked like a saner marker height under y_up:false; (b) a second rigid body ('block') read z=0.348 on a shelf then z=0.021 near the floor; (c) the user's OWN 'mushr2 yaw ~= 5 degrees' check was ALSO satisfiable under y_up:false + yaw_offset=pi (live yaw = -5.3 degrees). None of (a)-(c) are direct evidence of the rig's actual up-axis convention (raw-height heuristics can be misread, e.g. a marker mounted below a rigid body's own pivot, or a coincidentally-close yaw match under the wrong convention) -- if live data under y_up:true again looks physically wrong (heights below floor, etc.), get a fresh direct confirmation from the user of which axis is actually up in their Motive project rather than re-guessing from heuristics alone. A "Motive is Y-up" checkbox now also exists in mars_sim_viz's OptiTrack tab calibration UI (MARS/src/simviz/MocapTab.cpp) so this can be flipped with one click if the rig disagrees. RE-CORRECTED 2026-08-04 (transform-restructure session): this key's stored value had DRIFTED BACK to false despite this very doc entry saying "set back to true" -- almost certainly via mars_sim_viz's Calibration group 'Apply' button (MocapTab::on_apply_calibration()), which unconditionally rewrites x0/y0/theta0/y_up from whatever the GUI's four calibration fields currently show; those fields are only re-synced from disk at MocapManager construction and right after a successful Apply (see MocapTab::load_calibration_fields()), so a live mars_sim_viz session that was already running (or had been constructed) BEFORE this key was hand-corrected to true would still show the checkbox unchecked, and the next Apply click (e.g. to save an unrelated x0/y0/theta0 translation tweak) silently wrote y_up:false straight back over the fix, with no warning. Independently confirmed as a real, active bug (not just a hypothesis) by MPC/tests/test_optitrack_bridge.cpp's Part 1, which asserts an IDENTITY transform when no --map-config flag is passed (relying on optitrack_zmq_bridge's round-7 default-config-path fallback, which resolves to exactly this file) -- that assertion was actively FAILING (2040/2040 CSV rows mismatched) with y_up:false + theta0 nonzero (see the theta0 note below) before this correction. Fixed back to true here; MocapTab's stale-checkbox hazard itself is a separate, still-open GUI bug (the checkbox/spinboxes should be re-synced from the on-disk file immediately before Apply, not just at construction) -- flagged for a future session, out of scope for this transform-math task.
_doc.yaw_offset: Per-robot mounting-correction added to heading AFTER the global transform (matrix or legacy x0/y0/theta0) -- see optitrack_zmq_bridge.cpp's per-robot yaw_offset handling. Keys on the PUBLISHED name (e.g. "robot1", not Motive's raw "mushr2") in both explicit and auto-discovery mode. robot1's rigid body was created facing BACKWARD in Motive (confirmed live: the user's own 'yaw should read ~5 degrees' check only passes with this pi offset applied -- see the y_up entry above for the exact numbers) -- pi radians (180 degrees) corrects for that until refined by an actual motion-direction calibration (drive the robot forward, compare reported heading to the real heading of travel, adjust this value to close the gap exactly rather than relying on the approximate 5-degree check). NOTE (2026-08-04 transform-restructure session): this pi offset is consistent with a body created 180deg BACKWARD under the local-+X-is-forward assumption mocap_rotation()/quat_to_planar_yaw() use throughout -- there is no evidence of a 90deg (cross-axis, X-vs-Z-forward) convention mismatch that would call for a per-rig 'forward axis' config option; a 90deg error would show up as an offset near +-pi/2, not pi. RESET TO 0.0 (2026-08-04, later same day): per the user's explicit instruction 'make them 0 by default' -- now that the mocap transform chain above is corrected (y_up/theta0 drift fixed) and per-body yaw offsets are tunable LIVE from mars_sim_viz's OptiTrack-tab mapping-table UI (an editable per-row yaw-offset column, see MARS/src/simviz/MocapTab.cpp/MocapCore.h's set_yaw_offset()/set_yaw_offset_in_mapping()), there is no more need for a hand-edited pi-radian patch baked into this file as the default -- a user can dial in the real per-robot mounting correction from the GUI instead. The pi-radian history above is kept for context, not because pi is still believed correct.

_theta0_x0_y0_doc_correction_2026_08_04: theta0 had ALSO drifted (to pi, matching y_up's own drift -- see the y_up entry above) away from the IDENTITY (0,0,0) this file's own x0/y0/theta0 doc entry always claimed -- same root cause (a stale-checkbox Apply click writes all four calibration fields together). Restored to 0.0 here; independently confirmed broken via the same test_optitrack_bridge Part 1 regression (its 'no --map-config -> identity transform' assumption was failing 100% of CSV rows before this fix).
_doc_pose_filter: See doc/MOCAP_POSE_FILTER_PLAN.md for the full design/validation writeup. pose_filter is a per-body gated constant-velocity Kalman filter (mpc::PoseFilter, MPC/include/mpc/PoseFilter.h) that runs at the full 120Hz mocap frame rate and rejects single-(or few-)frame pose jumps before they ever reach mpc_controller/the GUI/mpc_tune. Ships DISABLED (enabled=false) pending: (a) a real captured jump turned into a regression fixture, (b) a hardware A/B (filter on vs off) showing tracking metrics unchanged within noise on clean data -- see the plan doc's 'Validation gate before enabling by default' checklist. Override live via --pose-filter on|off without editing this file. The values below are this feature's shipped defaults (data-driven off the 2026-08-28 robot2 rig recording, see the plan doc); --pose-filter on / enabled:true here starts using them.
